column1: # What the upstream-drift workflow watches, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/check-upstream.sh reads this; it knows how to query each ecosystem but nothing about which
# components this repository binds. Adding a native SDK means adding a row here.
# Columns are single-tab-separated.
#   group    reporting group - one GitHub issue per group, titled with this text
#   label    how the component is named inside the issue
#   kind     cocoapods | maven | github-release | github-tag
#   pin      the MSBuild property in Directory.Build.props holding the pinned version
#   locator  kind-specific: pod name, groupId:artifactId[:packaging][@repo], or owner/repo
#   confirm  download URL template with {version}, or "-" to derive it from the locator
# Only the Video SDK drives drift here. Its release notes are the reference for what changed:
# https://developer.vonage.com/en/video/client-sdk/android/release-notes
# WebrtcVersion is *derived*, not independently upgradable: it has to equal whatever
# opentok-android-sdk was built against, which its POM declares. Central carrying a higher
# com.vonage:webrtc is not an upgrade path - adopting it would desync the
# AndroidIgnoredJavaDependency in OpenTok.Net.Android.csproj from what the SDK actually pulls. So
# the webrtc row asks "does the pin match the bound SDK?" rather than "is there a newer one?",
# which is silent today (2.34.1 declares 121.1.101, which is what is pinned) and speaks up exactly
# when an OpenTok bump moves webrtc and this pin is left behind.
# group
